commit.message:
Fix rate limiter delaying tasks in a fresh window when `intervalCap > 1`

The fix for #182 tracked `#lastExecutionTime` to enforce spacing after the
queue went idle, but that anchor overshoots the real window boundary when
more than one slot is consumed per interval, blocking tasks that belong to
a fresh window.

Keep `#intervalEnd` accurate across window transitions instead and drop the
`#lastExecutionTime` guard entirely.

Fixes #251

Refine fresh-window rate limiter fix after review

Only advance `#intervalEnd` from the recurring interval timer, not from the
timeout-resume path. Advancing it there made the follow-up `#processQueue`
schedule a redundant timeout that coexisted with the `setInterval` created by
`#initializeIntervalIfNeeded`, causing extra window-boundary churn. The timeout
path already gets an accurate `#intervalEnd` from `#initializeIntervalIfNeeded`.

Also strengthen the issue #251 test to assert the full `intervalCap` is
available in the fresh window, and tidy a comment and a redundant ternary.

Document interval state machine and add fresh-window edge-case tests

Add field-level comments explaining the `#intervalEnd`/`#intervalId`/`#timeoutId`
interval state machine and why the fixed-window pause check only applies while
the queue is idle, since that invariant is what the issue #251 fix depends on.

Add two tests: one asserting a fresh window after idle still enforces the cap
for the following task (guarding against over-correction into always-allow), and
one covering the `carryoverIntervalCount` path through the fresh-window reset.

Add fresh-window rate limiter edge-case tests

Cover two paths the existing suite missed: a task added after the queue goes
idle but before the window boundary must still wait for the current window
(guarding against the reset firing too eagerly), and the strict-mode analog
where spread ticks age out individually so a slot frees mid-window.

Unwrap hard-wrapped comments
